{{Quote|I ain't afraid of Wookiees. It's their bowcasters that scare me.|Anonymous [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] slaver|<ref name="New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology" />}}
The '''bowcaster''' (sometimes called the '''Wookiee Crossbow''') was a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] projectile weapon that fired a metal [[Quarrel/Legends|quarrel]] enveloped in energy. Some bowcasters were modified to fire pure energy. Some variants had a capacity of twenty-four shots.

==Description==
{{Quote|I've always admired these Wookiee bowcasters. Artistry and firepower in one package.|[[Clone commando/Legends|Clone commando]] [[Boss (clone commando)/Legends|Boss]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Republic Commando">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Wookiee_swg.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Wookiee with a bowcaster.]]
In use as early as the [[Jedi Civil War]], the bowcaster could unleash a explosive bolt with impressive stopping power essential to defend Wookiees against the fierce predators of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk's]] [[Wroshyr tree/Legends|forests]].

The bowcasters were magazine-loaded with usually six to ten<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" /> explosive bolts per magazine. However some Wookiees developed a bowcaster that fired pure blaster bolts and no magazine was required.<ref name="TRG1-" /> A quiver of 10 quarrels cost 50 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] and weighed 1 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilogram]].<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" />

A polarizing orb sat at each end of the bow, generating a magnetic field used to accelerate the quarrels.<ref name="db">{{DB|technology|bowcaster|Wookiee bowcaster}}</ref> After cocking the weapon, a simple trigger sped the quarrel forward and charged it in an envelope of plasma. To generate the requisite potential energy for conversion into kinetic energy, the cocking spring required the strength of a Wookiee to draw back, although some modern bowcasters featured automatic cocking mechanisms for use by other species.<ref name="TRG1-" /><ref name="db" />

While decreasingly effective beyond 30 meters, the bowcaster was more powerful and accurate than typical [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] weapons. Some bowcasters could load multiple quarrels to create a spread-fire effect, further enhancing their close range effectiveness, while others could fire specially charged bolts that could ricochet off certain surfaces. They also shot pure bolts that were not engulfed in energy. These would sometimes have poison tips or explosive tips.
[[File:Embo-Encyclopedia.png|thumb|right|250px|Embo with his bowcaster variant]]
Bowcasters appeared huge to many non-Wookiees and even [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] such as [[Olee Starstone]] doubted they could lift one, much less fire it. The weight of the weapon, however, was no impediment to the massive strength of the Wookiees. In addition to its size, the exotic design of the bowcaster required a non-Wookiee user to have training in order to wield the weapon proficiently. One non-Wookiee individual who used a bowcaster was the [[Kyuzo/Legends|Kyuzo]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Embo/Legends|Embo]]. However, all Wookiees were able to wield their cultural weapon with proficiency.

Variants of the bowcaster included the [[Assault bowcaster]] used during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] and the [[Ceremonial bowcaster]] used in ceremonial hunts.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Bowcaster_egwt.png|thumb|left|150px|Bowcaster [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
The bowcaster was originally inspired by an illustration by John Schoenherr for George R.R. Martin's novelette "And Seven Times Never Kill a Man", published in the July 1975 issue of Analog, on which [[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s final [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] concept art was based.<ref name="BinaryBonsai">{{WebCite|url=http://binarybonsai.com/2010/09/18/george-lucas-stole-chewbacca-but-its-okay|text=George Lucas Stole Chewbacca, But It's Okay|work=binarybonsai.com|archivedate=20101009024242}}</ref>

Most sources, including [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], depict bowcasters firing green bolts. However, in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], Chewbacca's weapon fires red bolts and in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', Chewbacca's weapon fires yellow bolts. This is due to the [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] that Chewbacca made his out of a [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] rifle. In the ''[[Super Star Wars]]'' video game, Chewbacca's weapon looks like his usual bowcaster but is referred to as an [[FD-011 crossbow]].

In all ''Jedi Knight'' series of games, the bowcaster made an appearance. There, the user had two fire functions: one that could launch one to five bolts (depending on the amount of time spent charging up the shot) and one that launched a single, bouncing bolt. The latter was more accurate at far ranges, and could be fired at a faster pace. In both ''Jedi Knight/Dark Forces'' and ''Knights of the Old Republic'' games Wookiees are not the only bowcaster users. Many non-Wookiee mercenaries, bounty hunters, smugglers were equipped with this weapon in games, so did both Kyle and Jaden. Players are given the option of equipping [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] with bowcasters. All Wookiee player characters in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' start with the ability to craft bowcasters. In ''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]'', [[Darman Skirata]] states that the bowcaster is his favorite weapon.

There are significant differences in this weapon's range presented in the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]'' that differ from the range as listed in the ''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''. Instead of an optimum and maximum range of 30 and 50 meters respectively, the Saga Edition treats the bowcaster as a rifle, giving it an optimum and maximum range 90 and 450 meters respectively. This is probably due to the fact that the role-playing game data is heavily simplified and modified for ease of play.
